ratchet_note: detent-core and crates/modules are gated at 100% (PLAN §6.2). detent-platform is gated at 92, the floor that holds on Linux, which is where CI measures: macOS reads 97.5% but Linux reads 92.55% (5031/5436) because most of the crate's privileged code runs in a forked child. A child terminates with _exit(2), which skips the atexit handler LLVM installs to flush counters, so its lines read as uncovered even though they ran. privsep::sys::exit_immediately now calls __llvm_profile_write_file() first under cfg(coverage) (cargo-llvm-cov compiles with --cfg=coverage; production builds contain neither the declaration nor the call), which recovered privsep/sys.rs 30->46% and privsep/spawn.rs 75->82%. The remainder is irreducible with this approach: sandbox/linux.rs sits at ~55% because those children exit *after* confinement, and writing a profile needs openat/write, which the installed seccomp filter denies — flushing there would kill the child instead of measuring it. Those paths are verified by kernel-observable effects instead (EACCES on Landlock-denied writes, EPERM/SIGSYS from seccomp, the CapBnd bitmask in /proc/self/status), and they exit via exit_immediately_unflushed, which is documented as the only safe choice once a filter is installed. If this floor ever needs raising, the option not taken was __llvm_profile_set_file_object() with a descriptor opened before confinement plus a write allowance in the seccomp table — rejected for now as added complexity in security-critical code for a measurement-only benefit. detent-web enters at 97 (Phase 4a: config, TLS, headers, engine bridge). PLAN's Phase 4 acceptance is 100%, and this floor rises with each Phase 4 subtask; what is missing today is error paths that need a failing syscall to reach — getrandom failing, accept(2) erroring, a handshake timing out, a graceful-shutdown grace window expiring — plus the tracing access-log call, which emits nothing with no subscriber installed. detent-acme enters at 87 (Phase 6), measuring 87.85 on macOS; the one-point margin matches the Linux/macOS spread noted above. The gap is order.rs at 49%: present_challenges, present_attest_challenges, wait_ready and finalize all take an `instant_acme::Order`, which cannot be constructed without a live ACME client, so they are exercised only by tests/pebble_live.rs (#[ignore], needs PEBBLE_URL). Everything reachable without a network is covered, including the credential-cache branch that must not mistake an unreadable account file for a missing one — account_and_order refuses before it builds a client precisely so that branch is testable where both rustls providers are compiled in. providers.rs sits at 95% and is behind the off-by-default `dns-providers` feature until detent-acme links an HTTPS client. This floor rises when Phase 6 wiring gives the order flow a seam that fixtures can drive.
